title: Australian Sports Commission and Getty Images partner to change the face of Australian sport
summary: The Australian Sports Commission (ASC) and Getty Images have launched a new library of authentic images and videos to shift representation of Australian sport.
body_markdown:

Australian Sports Commission and Getty Images partner to change the face of Australian sport


Nov 23, 2026


|[PDF](https://newsroom.gettyimages.com/en/getty-images/australian-sports-commission-and-getty-images-partner-to-change-the-face-of-australian-sport/pdf)


*In support of Play Well, Australia’s Sport Participation Strategy, the partnership gives sports organisations access to a new visual library representing the real faces and aspects of Australian sport.*


**Sydney – November 24, 2026:** The Australian Sports Commission (ASC) and[Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/) , the preeminent source of authentic visual content and coverage, have launched a new library of authentic images and videos to shift representation of Australian sport. In the lead‑up to the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, the library provides sporting organisations with imagery and video that supports the Play Well vision that everyone has a place in sport.


To reflect the full breadth of Australian communities, Getty Images worked with community sports clubs participants and ASC networks to create visual stories from across the country. Partners included Sport Inclusion Australia, which supports people with an intellectual disability to access sport at every level, and the Metropolitan Districts Netball Association (QLD), with everyday Australians documented at their local clubs.


The library is made up of newly commissioned imagery and video shot by exclusive photographers and videographers via Getty Images’[Custom Content](https://www.gettyimages.com.mx/enterprise/custom-content) offering. It is free for the ASC and its partner organisations to use, and available to license for commercial use by sports organisations, media and brands worldwide, exclusively through GettyImages.com. Imagery features a range of Australians across athletics, equestrian, netball, badminton and soccer, and responds to representation gaps identified through the Play Well Strategy and Getty Images VisualGPS research.


The visual library currently has over 1500+ assets across stills and videos, with more sports to be added to the platform throughout 2027.


**Svetlana Zhukova, Senior Director of Custom & Creative Partnership at Getty Images, said:** *“Sport has an extraordinary ability to connect people, but the images used to represent it don’t always reflect who is actually taking part. Visuals shape perceptions of who belongs, often in ways people don’t consciously notice. Through the partnership, we’re giving sports organisations, media and communities access to the imagery that better reflects the diversity of Australian sport as the country looks towards Brisbane 2032.”*


Launched in 2023 and co‑designed with the Australian sport sector, Play Well supports organisations and initiatives working to get more Australians into sport, making sure people of all ages, genders, backgrounds and abilities can access its benefits.


**Richard McInnes, Executive General Manager of Sport System Impact at Australian Sports Commission, and Chair of the Play Well Leadership Group, said:** *“Play Well is centred on the belief that everyone has a place in sport, and this project proudly reflects that. This strategy is about breaking down barriers to involvement and we’re taking action by identifying the gaps that exist to ensure modern Australia is reflected. The partnership with Getty Images gives us a practical way to do that by celebrating the people, connections and authentic stories that underpin Australian sport.”*


Getty Images’[VisualGPS](https://www.gettyimages.com.mx/visualgps) research shows why this work matters. **59% of Australians agree that sports organisations, leagues and brands could do more to promote the diversity of their players** , and **56% say more people would consider taking part if the industry did a better job of including people from diverse backgrounds in ownership, leadership, coaching and employment.**


**Chantel Lewis, Chief Executive Officer of Sport Inclusion Australia, said:** *“Inclusion should be embedded in everything we do in sport from the very beginning, not something we consider or add later. That includes how we design programs, create opportunities, communicate and represent the people who make up our sporting communities. Sport has the power to bring people together, but for people to feel they belong, they first need to see that sport is for them.”*


*“The images and stories we share play an important role in challenging perceptions, breaking down barriers and showing that people with an intellectual impairment, including intellectual disability and/or autism, are part of the Australian sporting landscape. Sport Inclusion Australia is proud to partner with the Australian Sports Commission and Getty Images on this initiative. It's an important step towards ensuring the diversity of Australian sport is genuinely reflected and encouraging sporting organisations to make inclusion part of everything they do, at every level of sport.”*
